findings.claim: The origin queue rejects a second dispatch for the same signed request ID, which prevents a single remote request from being delivered to multiple target peers and breaks per-peer aggregation.
findings.evidence: In `accept_verified_unlocked`, after accepting one dispatch, the queue iterates all records and returns `RemoteError::RequestReplay` whenever `existing.dispatch.request.request_id == dispatch.request.request_id`, regardless of target endpoint; acceptance criteria require per-peer receipt aggregation and mixed-target outcomes (`2.3 Implement ... per-peer terminal receipt aggregation`, `execution-remote-dispatch` scenario: "WHEN one target returns a verified receipt and another rejects authorization THEN aggregate status exposes both outcomes").
findings.suggested_fix: Deduplicate by dispatch ID/hash and by `(request_id, target_endpoint_id)` or another per-target key, not by request ID alone, so the same canonical request can be durably tracked for each enrolled target while still rejecting conflicting replays for the same target.
